run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: All three requested queries were run against the cluster's Elasticsearch, and each returned zero only because the field named in the request does not exist in that index; re-running on the field the mapping actually defines produced non-zero counts. Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 has no `level` field (its severity field is the keyword `severity`): `term level=ERROR` returned 0 (also true across the whole authorized window), while `term severity=ERROR` returned 10 of the index's 16 documents. Index app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 has no `level` field either; its severity is the integer `severity_num`, with observed codes 3 (5 docs, messages prefixed `[INFO]`), 5 (6 docs, messages prefixed `[ERROR]`) and 6 (2 docs, messages prefixed `[FATAL]`), so the ERROR+FATAL equivalent of the requested terms query is 6+2 = 8 of 13 documents (the literal `terms level=[ERROR,FATAL]` query returned 0 over the whole window). Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no `@timestamp` field at all (no date-typed field in its mapping, so the tool applied no time filter); the timestamp is the keyword string field `ingest_ts`. A range over `@timestamp` for 2026-11-23 returned 0, whereas the same day's range on `ingest_ts` (2026-11-23T00:00:00 to 23:59:59) returned 11 documents, of which `level=ERROR` matched 7 (the other 4 are INFO; the index's 16 documents split 12 ERROR / 4 INFO overall). All figures are counts of documents matching the query in the searched index and window; they are log-document counts, not request or error rates, and nothing here shows service health.

claims.text: The cluster contains exactly three indices matching app-280-logs-*: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 (16 docs), app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 (13 docs), app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 (16 docs), all open and green.

Mappings: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 has @timestamp(date), message(text), service(keyword), severity(keyword); app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 has @timestamp(date), msg(text), severity_num(integer), svc(keyword); app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has ingest_ts(keyword), level(keyword), message(text) — no @timestamp and no date-typed field.

Q1 as asked: term {level:"ERROR"} on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0 (tool auto-filtered @timestamp to 2026-11-23T17:18:09Z–18:18:09Z), and it also returned 0 when widened to the full authorized window 2026-10-24T18:18:09Z–2026-11-23T18:18:09Z, consistent with `level` not existing in that index.

Q1 re-run on the correct field: term {severity:"ERROR"} on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 matched 10 documents in the full authorized window, and a match_all severity aggregation over the same index/window shows severity buckets ERROR=10 and INFO=6 out of 16 documents (returned document times span 2026-11-03T22:14:01Z to 2026-11-03T22:15:06Z, i.e. outside the default 1-hour window).
Q2 as asked: terms {level:["ERROR","FATAL"]} on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 returned 0 both in the default 1-hour window and over the full authorized window; that index has no `level` field.

Q2 severity field discovery: the severity label is the integer severity_num in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3; a terms aggregation over all 13 documents in the full authorized window yields code 5 = 6 docs, code 3 = 5 docs, code 6 = 2 docs.

Q2 code semantics observed in messages: severity_num 3 documents read "[INFO] healthcheck …"; severity_num 5 documents read "[ERROR] DB timeout …" (6 such docs, e.g. @timestamp 2026-11-23T18:14:05Z–18:14:06Z); severity_num 6 documents read "[FATAL] Disk full …" (2 such docs, 2026-11-23T18:15:01Z–18:15:02Z).

Q3 as asked: range on @timestamp for 2026-11-23 (00:00:00Z–23:59:59Z) combined with level=ERROR in app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 returned 0, and a bare range on @timestamp for that day also returned 0; the tool reported "No matched index maps a date field, so no time filter was applied", i.e. @timestamp does not exist in this index.

Q3 re-run on the correct timestamp field: range {ingest_ts: gte 2026-11-23T00:00:00, lte 2026-11-23T23:59:59} AND level=ERROR in app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 matched 7 documents; the same range without the level filter matched 11 documents (level buckets ERROR=7, INFO=4).

app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 contains 16 documents split level ERROR=12 and INFO=4, with ingest_ts values 2026-11-22T08:01:00–08:05:00 (5 docs) and 2026-11-23T08:01:00–08:07:00 plus 09:01:00–09:04:00 (11 docs); ingest_ts is a keyword string with minute precision and no timezone suffix.

The zeros in questions 1–3 are not evidence that the logs contain no errors: after switching to the mapped fields, the same indices returned 10 ERROR docs (a), 8 ERROR/FATAL docs (b) and 7 ERROR docs on 2026-11-23 (c).

For these three indices, change the queries to the fields the mappings actually define: severity on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, severity_num (3=INFO, 5=ERROR, 6=FATAL as observed in msg prefixes) on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, and ingest_ts on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3; pass explicit start_time/end_time wider than the tool's default 1-hour window, since index a's documents all lie on 2026-11-03 and are invisible in a 1-hour window ending 2026-11-23T18:18:09Z.

gaps: No stored severity-code dictionary was found: the mapping 3=INFO, 5=ERROR, 6=FATAL for severity_num in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 is inferred from the msg text prefix of a sample (2 docs for code 5, 2 docs for code 6, 3 docs for code 3), not from an explicit field or lookup; a document whose msg prefix disagreed would change the ERROR+FATAL count of 8.

app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no date-typed field, so Elasticsearch applies no time filter to it and documents cannot be proven to fall in any incident window by timestamp type; ingest_ts is a keyword string of minute precision without timezone, and the "today" boundary was taken as 2026-11-23T00:00:00–23:59:59 by lexicographic string range on the assumption that it represents UTC.

Document totals are what these queries matched now; documents deleted or added after the searches, and any documents outside the authorized window 2026-10-24T18:18:09Z–2026-11-23T18:18:09Z, are unknown (index doc counts 16/13/16 come from the index listing at query time).

Two exploratory calls were rejected by the gateway with INVALID_PARAMS (a source-filtered document fetch as a JSON string array, and a match_all with source array), so those views yielded nothing; the same samples were obtained with an includes-object source filter instead.

No service health, error-rate or request-level conclusion is supported here: only log-document counts in the three named indices were examined, and no Kubernetes, Prometheus or trace data was queried because the request was limited to Elasticsearch counts.
next_steps: Confirm the numeric severity scale used by the writer of app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 (for example from the application's logging configuration or pipeline), so 5/6 can be mapped to ERROR/FATAL with certainty.
If per-day error trends are needed for app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, consider indexing ingest_ts as a date field rather than a keyword string so time filters and date_histogram work reliably.
Re-scope the index 'a' queries to the date range containing its documents (around 2026-11-03) when comparing counts across the three indices.
